questions.q: What does the summary say people dislike even more than making a mistake?
a: Admitting that they made it
Repeating the same mistake
Hiding it from other people
Being blamed for it publicly
questions.why: The first lesson argues that admitting errors is the hardest and most necessary step.

questions.q: Why did it take so long to test the DNA evidence in Juan Rivera's case?
a: Prosecutors could not face admitting a grave mistake
The evidence had been destroyed years earlier
The testing technology did not yet exist
Rivera refused to cooperate with testing
questions.why: The summary says admitting the error would have cost the prosecutors their jobs and confidence.

questions.q: What does treating your ideas as hypotheses encourage you to do?
a: Look for evidence that contradicts them
Defend them more confidently in debate
Simplify them until they are easy to explain
Act on them before doubts set in
questions.why: The summary contrasts this with seeking only confirmation of what you already believe.

questions.q: What does the bloodletting example warn against?
a: Assuming a common practice must be right without testing it
Trusting modern medicine over traditional remedies
Ignoring a patient's symptoms during treatment
Adopting new technology too quickly
questions.why: Doctors never tested bloodletting because it seemed obviously cleansing, and it killed people.

questions.q: Why do some students party before an exam, according to the summary?
a: They sabotage themselves so failure can be blamed on partying
They are confident they will pass without studying
They focus better under last-minute pressure
They want to calm their nerves before the test
questions.why: The summary calls this a loser's attitude: it protects them from falling short of expectations.
